quote.text: It’s something like going on an ocean voyage. What can I do? Pick the captain, the boat, the date, and the best time to sail. [11] But then a storm hits. Well, it’s no longer my business; I have done everything I could. It’s somebody else’s problem now – namely the captain’s. [12] But then the boat actually begins to sink. What are my options? I do the only thing I am in a position to do, drown – but fearlessly, without bawling or crying out to God, because I know that what is born must also die.
quote.author: Epictetus
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood:
    • Just as you choose the ship and the voyage, you decide the values and lessons you wish to embed in your child’s life. Your guidance shapes their journey even when unforeseen storms arise.
    • When challenges in raising a child emerge—unexpected tantrums or adverse influences—remember that you have done your due diligence. Trust in the foundation laid, and accept that some struggles fall beyond your direct control.
  • Leadership:
    • In leadership, selecting the right team and strategy mirrors picking the best times to sail. Commit wholeheartedly to your decisions and prepare as best as possible, knowing that external forces may still disrupt your plans.
    • When turbulence hits—a crisis or unforeseen setback—maintain calm and accountability. Lead by example through resilience, showing that even in the midst of a storm, a rational mind does not cower, but acts with measured resolve.
  • Product Management:
    • Planning a product launch resembles setting out on an ocean voyage. Research, strategy, and risk assessments are like choosing the captain and the boat. Yet, market shifts and unexpected challenges remind us that not everything is within our control.
    • When a crisis emerges, whether it’s a failing feature or a shifting customer need, face it with stoic acceptance. Execute your responsibilities methodically and understand that some outcomes require adaptation and responsibility from others in the collective decision-making process.
